messages:
Noah (New Hire): Hi everyone, quick onboarding/payroll/benefits things I ran into this morning:
1) My benefits email shows coverage starting 2024-06-01 but my offer said immediate coverage. Is that a vendor timing thing or a setup bug?
2) My address in ADP is my old address; I updated it but payroll still used the old state for tax withholdings. Who do I need to talk to to get that corrected retroactively?
3) I tried adding my child as a dependent but the portal rejected the birth certificate upload with a vague "document mismatch" error. Any tips?

Sasha (People Ops): Welcome Noah! :wave: Short answers:
1) Coverage often shows first of next month if eligibility date is after the monthly cutover. We can request expedited enrollment for new hires in certain cases. DM me your employee ID and I can escalate to the carrier.
2) Address changes in ADP should propagate but if payroll already ran with the old state we can file a retro tax change. @Gabe can confirm the process and any forms needed (state W-4 or local equivalent).
3) Dependent docs: portal expects either a certified birth certificate (PDF) or passport. Make sure the file is a searchable PDF or an image (PNG/JPG). If it's scanned, try rescanning at 300dpi and remove encryption. If it still errors, DM me the filename and I'll trigger a manual vendor upload.

Noah (New Hire): Thanks Sasha. Gabe, can you say what happens if payroll already withheld state tax for the wrong state? Is that something I have to claim on my state return or do you handle it?

Gabe (Payroll): Hey Noah  if payroll withheld the wrong state tax because of the address mismatch we can submit an amended payroll to credit the difference, but timing matters. If the incorrect withholding happened this pay period we can adjust in the next run if you report it before cutoff (Fri 6pm PST). If it's been several cycles we typically advise filing for a refund with the state, but we can assist with documentation. DM me pay dates and the incorrect state and I'll take a look.

Noah (New Hire): Cool, I'll pull the paystub and DM you. On the expedited benefits: what qualifies as "certain cases"? I had a planned surgery and need coverage in 2 weeks.

Ivy (Benefits): Hi Noah  medical urgency can sometimes justify expedited enrollment, carriers vary. Upload the surgery scheduling note or a provider letter to the benefits portal and tag me; I'll open an exception request. If approved, coverage can be backdated to your eligibility date in some cases. Keep in mind carrier approvals aren't guaranteed.

Noah (New Hire): Ok uploading provider note now. Also the portal asked for a dependent SSN for my child but we don't have one yet (born overseas). Is that okay?

Sasha (People Ops): You can enroll the child pending SSN in most cases; use "SSN pending" field where available and upload a passport/birth cert. Some carriers require SSN within 30-60 days. We'll put a follow-up task on your profile so we don't lose the enrollment.

Noah (New Hire): Appreciate it. One more small Q: holiday allotment  my offer lists 5 floating days but the ADP shows 3. Is that a pro-rate thing or bug?

Sasha (People Ops): Floating days are pro-rated based on your start date and FTE. If your offer explicitly promised 5 for the calendar year, DM me the offer text and I'll reconcile with payroll/comp. Otherwise you were likely prorated because you started after the quarter start.

Onboarding Bot: Reminder: benefits dependent documentation window closes 30 days after eligibility. Missing SSN must be updated within 60 days to prevent carrier audit. See https://benefits.redwood.com/enrollment for details.

Gabe (Payroll): Adding: please DM me the check dates and your ADP change timestamp. If you updated address before payroll cutoff we may be able to re-run state withholding without manual forms. If after cutoff we'll file a retro and coordinate with tax team.

Noah (New Hire): Thanks y'all. I'll DM docs and paystub now. Really appreciate the quick turnaround during my first week! :thumbsup:
